question_record.context: A security incident was reported where emails containing a malicious URL `https://ym018491661.wittytree-b6f239d6.northeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/` were delivered to and later removed from the mailbox of `bjenkins@niseko.alpineskihouse.co`. The email was sent from `santiago@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` with the sender IP `119.36.50.193`. This incident involves the user account `Lucas Grey` with email `Lucas Grey@niseko.alpineskihouse.co`.
question_record.question: During the investigation of the incident, a suspicious sequence of exploration activities was detected. Can you provide the Security Identifier (Sid) of the account involved in these suspicious activities?
solution: The email account with SID `S-1-5-21-561436748-3867387497-1732241745-3701` received an email with a malicious URL that was delivered and later removed.
A process `powershell.exe` scanned or dumped memory from the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe), potentially allowing the attacker to extract authentication hashes or passwords.

The account with SID `S-2-5-21-571436798-3864380397-1837441745-3206` executed a suspicious sequence of windows commands to identify assets of value and coordinate lateral movement after compromising a machine.

92.name: Email messages containing malicious URL removed after delivery​
92.description: Emails with malicious URL that were delivered and later removed -V62.34.26.163

67.name: Sensitive credential memory read
67.description: A process scanned or dumped memory from the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe).  Accessing this process memory allows the attacker to extract secrets such as authentication hashes or passwords.  A copy of this memory may be written to the file system and exfiltrated to extract these credentials offline.

52.name: Suspicious sequence of exploration activities
52.description: A process called a set of windows commands. These commands can be used by attackers in order to identify assets of value and coordinate lateral movement after compromising a machine.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Account_Derived_Email' AND o.Concept = 'Account_SID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
